text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Governor of Bosnian National bank, Kasim Omicevic, says currency law will be adopted in the next few days.

- A Bosnian army senior officer who asked not to be named told newspaper that federation army will be reorganised with three corps instead of the existing five. Croatian militia forces integrated within the federation army will have only one corps in Herzegovina in southwest Bosnia.
- Bosnia's Council of Ministers adjourned four-hour session after failing to adopt working rules. It agreed to meet again next Thursday.
- U.S. Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum met Bosnian foreign affairs minister Jadranko Prlic. They discussed possibilities for Bosnia to become part of NATO Partnership for Peace programme.
- Bosnian Interior Minister Muhamed Zilic announced that new police forces will be reduced by 25 to 30 percent, which will require laying off 5,000 policemen.
- An educational pilot-project to train secretaries will start in February with donation of Iranian government. Some 120 young women, mostly refugees and displaced persons, will participate.
- Opposition parties from the Moslem-Croat Federation and the Serb Republic said they were planning to form a shadow cabinet that would try to build political consensus in country.
- Three months after signing protocol on Sarajevo cantonal administration, nothing has been done to establish city authorities, Croat member of the three-man Bosnian Presidency, Kresimir Zubak said.

- Judges for Moslem-Croat Fedration Supreme Court and public prosecutors were sworn in on Monday. Paper said inauguration represents additional step towards rebuilding confidence among ethnic groups by establishing rule of law.
- Bosnian civil engineering company "Bosna" says it has resumed production with 700 employees, including demobilised soldiers.
